text:
maria: Heads-up — after the kernel-selection change merged yesterday I'm seeing host-side P95 regression (~+18ms) on short-seq traffic under bursts. Not sure if it's batching heuristics or KV cache churn. cc @sam @josh

sam: ugh, saw alerts too. stack: ingress parse -> tokenizer -> routing -> runtime kernel pick -> kvcache lookup -> decode. Which path did you profile?

maria: quick flame showed CPU in parse/tokenize and a surprising spike in small write syscalls around the grpc layer. Also lots of repeated kvcache misses on overlapping prefixes. paste of the perf sample:

```
Samples: 120K of event 'cpu-clock'
# Overhead  Command  Shared Object  Symbol
  37.1%  runtime  libhostparse.so  host_parse_stream
  21.4%  runtime  libtokenizer.so  tokenize_short_seq
  12.0%  runtime  libgrpc.so    grpc_writev
  10.5%  runtime  libruntime.so  kernel_selector::pick_fast_path
```

josh: interesting that kernel_selector shows up — we recently added a shallow heuristics pass that prefers the new fused-attn kernel for sequences <64 because of throughput numbers on dedicated rigs. Might be causing odd micro-batching interactions.

irene: I can reproduce locally using the kbench reproducer with burst=200 clients, seq_len=20. I see kvcache eviction rate jump in the same window. Reproducer command: `./kbench --burst 200 --seq 20 --streaming`

sam: two hypotheses: 1) fused-attn kernel increases per-request prep time (mem layout conversion) for short seqs, outweighing gains; 2) kernel choice changes timing so requests land on kvcache hotset differently, causing KV churn and grpc writev fragmentation.

maria: perf-bot, can you attach the recent deploy hash and the kernel-selection diff?

perf-bot: deploy 2026-03-18T03:40Z sha=ab12f9. Kernel-selection change in diff: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/commit/ab12f9

josh: @maria @irene I ran a microtrace with wire-level capture. Key notes: when fused-attn chosen we do an extra memcpy into 32-byte aligned buffer before calling the kernel. That memcpy + small writev patterns in grpc explains the +10–15ms. Also I can see kvcache TTL bump because the ordering of requests changed — hot prefixes get evicted then re-requested.

maria: so recommended immediate mitigations?

sam: roll kernel-selection back to previous heuristics (disable fused-attn for seq<64) to validate. Also we can experiment with delaying memcpy until after batching (i.e., batch-concat then convert once).

irene: I pushed a canary patch that disables fused-attn on short seqs to canary hostpool A. Initial metrics look better — P95 back down ~9ms. Patching the batching heuristic could be lower-risk long-term.

josh: additional fix: coalesce small grpc writes into single writev per response; I have a small shim to aggregate chunk fragments on the host before sending. Might knock out the writev cost. Patch in review: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pull/782

maria: action items:
- @irene keep canary for 2h and run synthetic bursts (owner: irene)
- @josh finish writev coalesce shim + perf test (owner: josh)
- @sam prototype batching-change (owner: sam)
- @maria coordinate rollout/revert if canary fails and collect traces (owner: maria)

sam: one more note — KV cache tuning: bump max-entries for short-prefix hotset to reduce eviction during bursts. I'll model with current tail distribution and propose numbers.

maria: thanks team. if canary holds we can merge writev shim and a safer kernel-selection fix in the next patch. Will post update in 2h. :thumbsup:
